reading.title: A sugar tax that worked
reading.text: In 2018, the UK introduced a tax on sugary drinks. Instead of simply raising prices, the tax induced companies to change their recipes: many producers reduced the sugar in their drinks before the law even came into force. Researchers who conducted a study four years later found that children were consuming 30 percent less sugar from soft drinks. From this, they deduced that taxes aimed at producers can work better than campaigns to educate consumers. Critics replied that obesity rates had not yet fallen, and that education is still essential.
